newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil CVRD denies gold, copper discovery.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CVRD denies gold, copper discovery.

text.p: Brazil state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) has denied a newspaper report that the company had recently discovered "historic" gold and copper deposits.
"There has been no recent, surprising discovery, that does not exist," a CVRD spokesman said.

The report in today's edition of the O Estado de Sao Paulo said Vale geologists had found mineralised areas in the northern state of Para near the existing gold mine of Igarape Bahia and the Salobo gold, copper and silver project.
CVRD has been conducting further surveys near the Igarape Bahia gold mine which is currently Brazil's largest and produces around 10 tonnes a year, the spokesman said.
The mine is open-pit and CVRD has started to do some tests below the surface but this was already announced last year, the spokesman said.

"In July last year, we started doing some exploration...Of the six surveys, four reached gold so this is promising. But we would need to do 60 surveys. Today we do not know anything about what is under the surface," he said.

There is however no copper near the Igarape Bahia and the spokesman said the report of a copper discovery was being confused with the Salobo project, expected to see annual output of 525,000 tonnes of electrolytic copper, eight tonnes of gold and 37 tonnes of silver.
CVRD is one of the three companies involved in the mine, which should begin production in the year 2001.

The other two companies are the National Development Bank (BNDES) and Mineracao Morro Velho, controlled by the Brazilian arm of Minorco SA, which in turn is controlled by South Africa's Anglo-American and De Beers.
